text.student: On 3 February 1966 the Soviet probe Luna 9 made the first controlled soft landing on the Moon and sent back photographs of the surface, showing it was firm enough for landers.
text.explorer: Luna 9's capsule bounced and rolled after touchdown before settling in Oceanus Procellarum. Its panoramic pictures helped settle fears that landers would sink into deep lunar dust.

text.student: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed the lunar module Eagle in the Sea of Tranquility on 20 July 1969 and spent about two and a half hours outside.
text.explorer: Eagle touched down with Armstrong flying manually past a boulder field. The crew left a laser retroreflector that scientists still use to measure the Earth-Moon distance.

text.student: Pete Conrad and Alan Bean made a precision landing in the Ocean of Storms, within walking distance of the Surveyor 3 probe, and returned parts of it to study how materials age on the Moon.
text.explorer: Surveyor 3 had sat on the surface for about 31 months. Conrad and Bean retrieved its camera and tubing and set up the first nuclear-powered ALSEP science station.

text.student: Apollo 14 landed in the Fra Mauro highlands, the target of the cancelled Apollo 13. Alan Shepard famously hit two golf balls with a makeshift club.
text.explorer: Shepard and Edgar Mitchell collected about 42 kg of samples from the Fra Mauro formation, which is thought to be debris thrown out by the Imbrium basin impact.

text.student: Apollo 15 landed beside Hadley Rille and was the first mission to use the battery-powered Lunar Roving Vehicle, which let astronauts travel far from the lander.
text.explorer: David Scott and James Irwin spent about 18.5 hours outside over three moonwalks, drove roughly 28 km, and recovered the anorthosite nicknamed the Genesis Rock.

text.student: John Young and Charlie Duke made the only Apollo landing in the lunar highlands, to study the oldest parts of the Moon's crust.
text.explorer: The crew returned about 95 kg of samples. The highlands rocks were mostly impact breccias rather than the volcanic rocks scientists had expected.

text.student: Gene Cernan and geologist Harrison Schmitt were the last people to walk on the Moon, exploring the Taurus-Littrow valley.
text.explorer: Over three moonwalks totalling more than 22 hours they collected about 110 kg of samples, including orange volcanic glass soil spotted by Schmitt.

text.student: China's Chang'e 4 made the first soft landing on the Moon's far side and deployed the Yutu-2 rover.
text.explorer: The far side has no line of sight to Earth, so Chang'e 4 talks through the Queqiao relay satellite near the Earth-Moon L2 point.

text.student: Chandrayaan-3 was the first mission to soft-land near the lunar south pole. Its Vikram lander released the Pragyan rover.
text.explorer: It landed near 69.4 degrees south, closer to the pole than any earlier successful landing, close to craters in permanent shadow that may hold water ice.

text.student: Viking 1 landed in Chryse Planitia on 20 July 1976, photographed the surface and ran experiments looking for signs of life. It kept working for more than six years.
text.explorer: Its biology experiments gave ambiguous results that most scientists now attribute to reactive soil chemistry rather than living organisms.

text.student: Pathfinder landed with airbags on 4 July 1997 and carried Sojourner, the first wheeled rover to operate on Mars.
text.explorer: Sojourner weighed about 10.5 kg and operated for 83 sols, far longer than its planned 7.

text.student: Spirit landed in Gusev crater on 4 January 2004 and found silica-rich deposits that point to past water. It worked until 2010.
text.explorer: Spirit's wheel dragged up bright silica-rich soil, which usually forms in hot springs or steam vents, a sign of past water and heat.

text.student: Opportunity landed in Meridiani Planum and found hematite spheres and rocks shaped by water. A giant dust storm ended the mission in 2018.
text.explorer: It drove 45.16 km, further than any other vehicle on another world, and found evidence of acidic groundwater at Meridiani.

text.student: Curiosity was lowered by a sky crane into Gale Crater and found that an ancient lake here had the ingredients life needs.
text.explorer: It is exploring the layers of Mount Sharp, whose sediments change from clays to sulfates as Mars dried out.

text.student: InSight placed the first seismometer on the surface of Mars to study the planet's interior.
text.explorer: It detected more than 1,300 marsquakes and measured the crust, mantle and core before dust on its solar panels ended the mission in December 2022.

text.student: Perseverance landed in an ancient river delta and is sealing rock samples in tubes. Ingenuity made the first powered flight on another planet.
text.explorer: Jezero held a lake and delta billions of years ago, making its deposits a good place to look for signs of past microbial life.

text.student: Zhurong landed in Utopia Planitia with the Tianwen-1 mission and studied the surface with ground-penetrating radar.
text.explorer: It went into planned hibernation in May 2022 for the Martian winter and has not resumed operations.
